data.narrative:
Quantum Motion is a Series C quantum computing company founded by John Morton and Simon Benjamin. The target operates within a sector comprising 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ. The company has raised $160M+ to date.

The valuation analysis applies stage-progression methodology, the only triangulation method with sufficient analytical support. Using total raised ($160M) as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, this method yields an implied valuation of $272M. The peer-median approach was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing sector—while 8 private peers exist sector-wide, none cluster sufficiently at similar valuation tiers or stages to produce a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $231M (low) to $313M (high), centered on $272M. This relatively tight band reflects reliance on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include calibration of the stage-progression multiplier to quantum computing's capital intensity and duration, the representativeness of total raised as a valuation proxy absent recent external pricing, and structural heterogeneity across the peer set regarding technology approach and commercialization timeline. A future Series C financing round or comparable transaction would substantially improve precision.
